headline: Referred resolution giving 142 South Bend Street to school committee for new high school; sent Rice Street stop sign request to Public Works.
summary: Referred a resolution giving the school committee site control of 142 South Bend Street for a new unified high school. Approved a request for stop signs and painted lines on Rice Street. Confirmed two Riverfront Commission members and approved one $281.27 claim payment.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda by unanimous voice vote, including filing communications and referring claims.
Approved the July 22, 2026 meeting records as prepared by the Clerk.
Referred resolution giving 142 South Bend Street site control to the City Property Committee for a new unified high school.
Referred damage claims by Juan Hernandez ($680.96) and Bernard Donald Grossi, Jr. ($140.00) to the Committee on Claims and Pending Suits.
Referred four damage claims against the city to the Law Department and RI Interlocal Trust.
Approved request to Public Works for stop signs and painted lines on Rice Street, by unanimous voice vote.
Confirmed reappointment of Michael A. Lafond to the Riverfront Commission, 8-0.
Confirmed appointment of David Sisson to the Riverfront Commission, 8-0.
Approved resolution moving the September 9, 2026 Board of License Commissioners and City Council meetings to September 10, 2026, 8-0.
Approved payment of $281.27 damage claim by Ashley Mazzucco, 8-0.
Denied $250.00 pothole damage claim by Christine King and referred it to the Pawtucket Water Supply Board, 8-0.

City Council, August 5, 2026 
 
A regular session of the Pawtuck et City Council was held Wednesday, August 5, 2026, at 
7:44 p.m., in the Temporary City Council Chambers, 2nd Floor, 100 Freight St. , Pawtucket, 
RI. 
 
Present – President Mercer; Councilors Araujo, Coderre, Moran, Moreno, Rubio, Stachowiak 
and Wildenhain. 
 
Absent – Councilor Gregor. 
 
President Mercer presided. 
 
The reading of the records of the July 22, 2026 City Council meeting was dispensed with and 
the records were APPROVED as prepared by the Clerk. 
 
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Araujo, seconded by Councilor  Moreno, the *Consent 
Agenda was APPROVED on a unanimous voice vote: 
 
 *THE FOLLOWING COMMUNICATIONS WERE READ AND ORDERED FILED 
  
 A. Publication from Megan Khatchadourian, Assistant to  the Director, RI ACLU to 
RI City and Town Councils and School Committees (Remote Access to Public 
Meetings) 
  
 B. Communication from Jason Pezzullo, Commerce Director, to the Honorable 
Members of the Pawtucket City Council (Reappointment of Jennifer Kilsey , 
Cultural Affairs Program Coordinator, to the Arts Panel Review Committee) 
  
 C. RESOLUTION PROVIDING SITE CONTROL OF 142 SOUTH BEND STREET 
TO THE PAWTUCKET SCHOOL COMMITTEE FOR THE CONSTRUCTION 
OF A NEW UNIFIED HIGH SCHOOL IN THE CITY OF PAWTUCKET – 
WAS REFERRED TO THE CITY PROPERTY COMMITTEE. 
  
 D. THE FOLLOWING CLAIM S FOR DAMAGES AGAINST THE CITY WAS 
REFERRED TO THE COMMITTEE ON CLAIMS AND PENDING SUITS: 
Juan Hernandez – $680.96 (Pothole) 
Bernard Donald Grossi, Jr. – $140.00 (Tow) 
  
 E. THE FOLLOWING CLAIM S FOR DAMAGES AGAINST THE CITY WAS 
REFERRED TO THE LAW DEPARTMENT AND RI INTERLOCAL TRUST: 
Zachary Fulford by Gianfrancesco, Friedemann & Maselli – No amount specified 
(Personal Injury) 
Margarita Cruz Serrano by Bottaro Law Firm, LLC – No amount specified 
(Personal Injury) 
Makayla Gomes by Robert Testa, Esq. – No amount specified (Personal Injury) 
Donnell Mitchell by Alexander Lebowitz, Esq. – No amount specified (Vehicle 
Damage/Personal Injury) 
 
 
THE COUNCIL TOOK UP THE FOLLOWING: 
 
Traffic Control issues on Rice Street (Stop Signs) 
 
THE CHAIR RECOGNIZED COUNCILOR MORAN 
 
With majority consent of the Council, the following motion made by Councilor  Moran, 
seconded by Councilors Araujo and Moreno, was PASSED on a unanimous voice vote: 
 
The Clerk was instructed  to send a communication to Chris Crawley, Acting Director of 
Public Works, requesting the installation of “Three-Way Stop” and “Four-Way Stop” signs, 
“Stop Sign Ahead ” signs, and painted traffic lines on Rice Street at  or near the intersections 
of Bart Dr., Archer St., and Weldon St., to help get people to stop at these intersections.
